items.title: Adoption of the external-torque branch of the rigid-material model: declared torque data and the balance of angular momentum about the centre of mass
items.statement:
Adopt as physical assumptions of the framework the following
**external-torque branch** of the rigid-material model, in the setting of
[[post-cm10-rigid-material]].

**(i) Setting.** A model of the branch carries the data of
[[post-cm10-rigid-material]]: a reference mass distribution $\nu$ with total
mass $m>0$ and centred reference coordinates, a time window $I_0$, an
inertial frame with adapted coordinates $(t,x)$ ([[post-cm01-frames]]), and a
motion $x(t,\rho)=c(t)+R(t)\rho$ with configuration path $(c,R)$ of class
$C^{2}$ ([[def-cm10-rigid-body-configuration]]). Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]), used only
through [[pthm-cm10-kinetic-splitting]] to make the defining integrals of the
model's inertial quantities finite. Along the motion the body angular
velocity $\omega$ and the body inertia matrix $I$ are those of
[[def-cm10-angular-velocity]] and [[def-cm10-inertia-tensor]], and the
**angular momentum about the centre of mass** is
$$L_c(t):=\int\bigl(x(t,\rho)-c(t)\bigr)\times\bigl(\partial_tx(t,\rho)-c'(t)\bigr)\,d\nu(\rho),$$
the finite vector of clause 1 of [[pthm-cm10-kinetic-splitting]], which by
clause 4 of that item satisfies the identity
$$L_c(t)=R(t)\,I\,\omega(t)\qquad(t\in I_0).$$

**(ii) External torque datum.** An **external torque datum** of the branch on
the time window $I_0$ is a continuous map
$$\tau:I_0\longrightarrow\mathbb R^3,\qquad [\tau]=\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2},$$
the dimension being read in newton metres ([[def-cm01-units]]). Its intended
physical reading is: $\tau(t)$ is the **total external torque about the
centre of mass** at time $t$, the resultant moment about $c(t)$ of the forces
external to the model that act on the body at time $t$: weight in a declared
gravitational field, forces exerted by supports, pivots, axles or contacts,
thrusts and drives, applied couples, and frictional torques. Which external
agencies occur and which datum they jointly produce is model data fixed by
the model's further assumptions; this postulate does not derive $\tau$ from
any force system, and the statements of the pair use $\tau$ only through the
balance below.

**(iii) The adopted balance.** Along every motion of a model of the branch
with external torque datum $\tau$, adopt the **external-torque balance**
$$L_c'(t)=\tau(t)\qquad(t\in I_0).$$
This is an adopted dynamical law of the model. Through the identity
$L_c=RI\omega$ of clause (i) it is one vector equation relating the
configuration path, its first two time derivatives and the datum; it does
not by itself determine $(c,R)$, and it is not a consequence of the kinematic
definitions of [[post-cm10-rigid-material]].

**(iv) Torque-free motions.** A model of the branch whose datum vanishes,
$\tau\equiv0$ on $I_0$, is called **torque-free**; for such a model the
balance reads $L_c'\equiv0$ on $I_0$. Torque-free is a property of the
declared datum, not of the mass distribution: every model of
[[post-cm10-rigid-material]] may be used with the zero datum, and the
statements of this page about torque-free motions are conditional on that
use.

**(v) Relation to the particle branch.** The framework's angular-momentum
balance for finitely many particle labels is
[[pthm-cm03-angular-momentum-balance]]: for a model that declares the
external-plus-pair presentation with antisymmetric pair forces, the angular
momentum about a fixed reference point has derivative equal to the total
torque about that point, the internal torque sum cancelling when the
evaluated pair forces are central. The rigid-material model has no particle
labels; its mass data are the measure $\nu$, and all its physical statements
weight material points by $\nu$. That balance is therefore not available
verbatim for the model of clause (i), and clause (iii) is adopted here as the
rigid-material analogue. No claim that clause (iii) follows from
[[pthm-cm03-angular-momentum-balance]], or from any other item of the
framework, is made by this postulate or proved anywhere on this page.

**(vi) No other balances.** This postulate asserts no balance for the total
momentum $mc'$ and no equation of motion for the centre of mass: an external
force datum is not part of the branch, the curve $c$ remains free except as
restricted by further model assumptions (for instance a pivot constraint
adopted on this page), and the theorems of the pair use only the balance
(iii). In particular the branch neither asserts nor denies that the centre of
masses moves uniformly, and it asserts no conservation of the rotational
kinetic energy; the power identity for the rotational term is a theorem of
this page, not an assumption.

**(vii) Frame consistency.** Let a second inertial frame be related to the
chosen one by the transformation $t'=t+b$, $x'=Qx+ut+a$ of
[[post-cm01-frames]] clause (iv), with $b\in\mathbb R$, $a,u\in\mathbb R^{3}$
and $Q\in SO(3)$, and let $\tilde x(t',\rho):=Q\,x(t'-b,\rho)+u\,(t'-b)+a$ be
the description of the same motion in the second frame
([[pthm-cm10-frame-covariance]] clause 1). Adopt: this description is again a
motion of the same model of the branch, and an external torque datum of the
model transforms between the two descriptions by
$$\tilde\tau(t'):=Q\,\tau(t'-b),$$
the transformation of a spatial vector under the rotation $Q$ alone, with no
contribution from the boost $u$, the translation $a$ or the time shift $b$.
The consistency of the balance (iii) with this transformation law — namely
that the description in the second frame satisfies the balance with datum
$\tilde\tau$, because
$\tilde L_c(t')=QL_c(t'-b)$ by clause 5 of
[[pthm-cm10-frame-covariance]] and differentiation commutes with the
constant rotation $Q$ and the time shift — is recorded and proved as a clause
of the frame-covariance theorem of this page; it is not an assumption of
the present postulate.

**(viii) Scope and exclusions.** The branch excludes deformable bodies,
internal degrees of freedom, variable mass, ablation, impact and contact
events, and every constitutive law for friction, rolling or slipping; any
such effect that is present must be declared as part of the datum $\tau$ of
clause (ii) with its own model, and a datum is a model object, not a
measurement. The branch also excludes relativistic and quantum descriptions.
Wherever a statement of the pair needs the inverse $I^{-1}$ it assumes the
model is nondegenerate in the sense of [[def-cm10-inertia-tensor]] clause
(a), and that hypothesis is stated explicitly in the theorem that uses it.
The postulate asserts no measured torque, no numerical value, and no claim
that any concrete body or apparatus is described by the branch; whether a
given datum is adequate for a given apparatus is decided by comparing the
model's conditional predictions with reported observations under the
apparatus's stated regime.
items.physical_scope: Adoption of the external-torque branch of the rigid-material model branch of [[post-cm10-rigid-material]]: a declared continuous external-torque datum $\tau:I_0\to\mathbb R^3$ (dimension $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$, newton metres), read as the total external torque about the centre of mass, and the adopted balance $L_c'=\tau$ of the angular momentum about the centre of mass. The postulate asserts no force law producing $\tau$, no balance for the centre-of-mass motion, no conservation law, no uniformity of rotation and no measured torque or observation; the countable-choice assumption is carried only for the finiteness of the defining integrals of the model's angular momentum. The branch excludes deformable bodies, impacts and variable mass; friction, contact and drive torques must be declared as part of $\tau$ with their own models.

items.title: Euler's equations with torque for the rigid-material model, the rotational power identity, the torque-free reduction and frame covariance
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]), used only through the integrals of
[[pthm-cm10-kinetic-splitting]]; the theorems below neither use nor imply any
other choice principle. Adopt a model of the rigid-material branch
[[post-cm10-rigid-material]] with the external-torque branch
[[post-cm11-torque-balance]]: a reference mass distribution $\nu$ with total
mass $m$ and centred reference coordinates, a time window $I_0$
([[def-interval]]), an inertial frame, a motion $x(t,\rho)=c(t)+R(t)\rho$ with
configuration path $(c,R)$ of class $C^{2}$
([[def-cm10-rigid-body-configuration]]), body angular velocity $\omega$
([[def-cm10-angular-velocity]]) and body inertia matrix $I$
([[def-cm10-inertia-tensor]]), and a continuous external torque datum
$\tau:I_0\to\mathbb R^{3}$ with respect to which the adopted balance of
[[post-cm11-torque-balance]] clause (iii) holds along the motion. Then:

1. **Euler's equations with torque.** Writing $l:=I\omega$, one has
   $l'=R^{\mathsf T}\tau-\omega\times I\omega$ and
   $$I\omega'(t)+\omega(t)\times I\omega(t)=R(t)^{\mathsf T}\tau(t)\qquad(t\in I_0).$$
2. **Principal-axis components.** If $(e_{1},e_{2},e_{3})$ is an orthonormal
   eigenbasis of $I$ with $Ie_{j}=I_{j}e_{j}$ ([[pthm-cm10-principal-axes]]
   clause (a)) and $\omega=\sum_{j}\omega_{j}e_{j}$,
   $R^{\mathsf T}\tau=\sum_{j}\tau_{j}e_{j}$, then the equations are
   componentwise
   $$I_{1}\omega_{1}'=(I_{2}-I_{3})\omega_{2}\omega_{3}+\tau_{1},\qquad I_{2}\omega_{2}'=(I_{3}-I_{1})\omega_{3}\omega_{1}+\tau_{2},\qquad I_{3}\omega_{3}'=(I_{1}-I_{2})\omega_{1}\omega_{2}+\tau_{3}.$$
3. **Rotational power identity.** The rotational kinetic energy
   $K_{\mathrm{rot}}(t):=\tfrac12\omega(t)^{\mathsf T}I\omega(t)$ is
   differentiable on $I_0$ with
   $$\frac{d}{dt}K_{\mathrm{rot}}(t)=\omega(t)\cdot R(t)^{\mathsf T}\tau(t)\qquad(t\in I_0);$$
   in particular, if $\tau\equiv0$, then $K_{\mathrm{rot}}$ is constant on
   $I_0$, and $K_{\mathrm{rot}}$ coincides with the rotational term
   $\tfrac12\omega^{\mathsf T}I\omega$ of the model's kinetic energy in
   clause 3 of [[pthm-cm10-kinetic-splitting]].
4. **Torque-free reduction and nondegeneracy.** Suppose $\tau\equiv0$ and the
   model is nondegenerate in the sense of [[def-cm10-inertia-tensor]] clause
   (a), so that $I$ is invertible with $I^{-1}l=\omega$. Then, writing
   $\omega$ as a function of $l$,
   $$l'=l\times(I^{-1}l),\qquad \omega'=F(\omega):=-I^{-1}\bigl(\omega\times I\omega\bigr);$$
   the second form exhibits the torque-free body angular velocity as a
   solution of the autonomous field $F$ on $\mathbb R^{3}$.
5. **Frame covariance.** Let a second inertial frame be related to the first
   by $t'=t+b$, $x'=Qx+ut+a$ with $b\in\mathbb R$, $a,u\in\mathbb R^{3}$,
   $Q\in SO(3)$ ([[post-cm01-frames]] clause (iv)), and let
   $\tilde x(t',\rho):=Qx(t'-b,\rho)+u(t'-b)+a$, $\tilde\tau(t'):=Q\tau(t'-b)$
   be the transformed motion and datum of [[post-cm11-torque-balance]] clause
   (vii). Then the balance holds in the second frame, and
   $$I\tilde\omega'(t')+\tilde\omega(t')\times I\tilde\omega(t')=\tilde R(t')^{\mathsf T}\tilde\tau(t')\qquad(t'\in I_0-b),$$
   where $\tilde\omega(t')=\omega(t'-b)$ and
   $\tilde R(t')=QR(t'-b)$; the body-frame torque is unchanged:
   $\tilde R(t')^{\mathsf T}\tilde\tau(t')=R(t'-b)^{\mathsf T}\tau(t'-b)$.

The statement is conditional on the adopted model and torque balance; it
asserts no force law for $\tau$, no conservation of $L_c$ and no measured
value.
items.physical_scope: Conditional deductions inside the external-torque branch of [[post-cm11-torque-balance]] for the rigid-material model of [[post-cm10-rigid-material]]: the body-frame Euler equations with the declared torque datum, their principal-axis components, the power identity $\frac{d}{dt}\tfrac12\omega^{\mathsf T}I\omega=\omega\cdot R^{\mathsf T}\tau$ (and constancy of the rotational kinetic energy in the torque-free case), the torque-free reduction $l'=l\times(I^{-1}l)$ under nondegeneracy, and the preservation of the balance under changes of inertial frame with the declared transformation of the torque datum. No force law producing $\tau$, no conservation of $L_c$ (which is proved on the same page), no measurement and no empirical value is asserted.

items.title: Torque-free motion of the rigid-material model: conservation of the angular momentum about the centre of mass, the energy-momentum invariants, the principal-axis equations and global existence of the spin dynamics
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]), used only through the integrals of
[[pthm-cm10-kinetic-splitting]]. Adopt a model of the rigid-material branch
[[post-cm10-rigid-material]] that is **nondegenerate** in the sense of
[[def-cm10-inertia-tensor]] clause (a) (no line through the origin carries
the whole mass), and use it in the **torque-free** external-torque branch of
[[post-cm11-torque-balance]] clause (iv): the datum vanishes, so along every
motion of the resulting model the adopted balance reads $L_c'=0$ on the time
window $I_0$. Let $\omega$ be the body angular velocity, $I$ the body inertia
matrix and $l:=I\omega$ ([[def-cm10-angular-velocity]],
[[def-cm10-inertia-tensor]]). Then:

1. **Conservation of angular momentum.** The angular momentum about the
   centre of mass $L_c(t)=R(t)l(t)$ of [[pthm-cm10-kinetic-splitting]] clause
   4 is constant on $I_0$; in particular $\lVert L_c\rVert_2$ is constant.
2. **Energy-momentum invariants and principal components.** The scalars
   $$C:=\langle l,l\rangle=\lVert L_c\rVert_2^{2},\qquad E:=\tfrac12\,\omega^{\mathsf T}I\omega=\tfrac12\,\langle l,I^{-1}l\rangle$$
   are constant on $I_0$, and $l$ satisfies the torque-free equation
   $$l'=l\times(I^{-1}l).$$
   If $(e_{1},e_{2},e_{3})$ is an orthonormal eigenbasis of $I$ with
   $Ie_{j}=I_{j}e_{j}$ and $l=\sum_{j}l_{j}e_{j}$
   ([[pthm-cm10-principal-axes]] clauses (a)-(b)), then
   $$C=\sum_{j}l_{j}^{2},\qquad E=\sum_{j}\frac{l_{j}^{2}}{2I_{j}},$$
   and the component equations are
   $$l_{1}'=\Bigl(\frac1{I_{3}}-\frac1{I_{2}}\Bigr)l_{2}l_{3},\qquad l_{2}'=\Bigl(\frac1{I_{1}}-\frac1{I_{3}}\Bigr)l_{1}l_{3},\qquad l_{3}'=\Bigl(\frac1{I_{2}}-\frac1{I_{1}}\Bigr)l_{1}l_{2}.$$
3. **The energy invariant is the rotational kinetic energy.** $E$ equals the
   rotational term $\tfrac12\omega^{\mathsf T}I\omega$ of the model's kinetic
   energy in clause 3 of [[pthm-cm10-kinetic-splitting]]; and with
   $I_{\min}:=\min_{j}I_{j}>0$ one has
   $$\lVert\omega(t)\rVert_2^{2}\le\frac{2E}{I_{\min}}\qquad(t\in I_0).$$
   In particular both $l$ and $\omega$ are bounded on $I_0$.
4. **The spin field is globally solvable.** The autonomous field
   $F(l)=l\times(I^{-1}l)$ on $\mathbb R^{3}$ is locally Lipschitz in the
   state variable ([[def-locally-lipschitz-in-the-state-variable]]), and
   every solution of $l'=F(l)$, with any datum in $\mathbb R^{3}$, is defined
   on all of $\mathbb R$ and satisfies $\lVert l(t)\rVert_2=\lVert l(0)\rVert_2$
   for every $t$. Consequently the $l$-path of a torque-free motion is the
   restriction to $I_0$ of a solution defined on all of $\mathbb R$, and its
   path is contained in the compact level set
   $$\Lambda(C,E):=\bigl\{z\in\mathbb R^{3}:\langle z,z\rangle=C,\ \tfrac12\langle z,I^{-1}z\rangle=E\bigr\},$$
   which is nonempty because it contains $l(0)$.

The statement is conditional on the adopted model, its nondegeneracy and the
zero-torque balance; it asserts no orientation of the body in space, no
measured value and no empirical law.
items.physical_scope: Conditional statements about a torque-free motion of a nondegenerate rigid-material model of [[post-cm10-rigid-material]]: the angular momentum about the centre of mass is constant in the inertial frame; the scalars $C=\lVert l\rVert_2^{2}=\lVert L_c\rVert_2^{2}$ and $E=\tfrac12\omega^{\mathsf T}I\omega=\tfrac12 l\cdot I^{-1}l$ are constants of the motion and $E$ is the rotational kinetic energy; in a principal basis the spin components obey the displayed torque-free equations; and the torque-free spin field is globally solvable in time, so the body angular momentum and the body angular velocity of a torque-free motion are bounded by initial data. The statements are conditional on the adopted zero-torque balance and nondegeneracy, carry the countable-choice assumption used only for the finiteness of the defining integrals, and assert no measurement, no orientation statement and no claim about nature.

items.title: Principal-axis uniform rotations of the torque-free rigid-material model: existence, the fixed spatial axis, the invariants, and the converse classification
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]), used only to select the initial unit quaternion
of [[def-cm-quaternion-rotation-map-and-cover]] through the surjectivity of
the double cover (its second remark). Adopt a **nondegenerate** model of the
rigid-material branch [[post-cm10-rigid-material]]: a reference mass
distribution $\nu$ with total mass $m$, centred reference coordinates and no
line through the origin carrying the whole mass
([[def-cm10-inertia-tensor]] clause (a)). Fix an orthonormal principal basis
$(e_{1},e_{2},e_{3})$ with $Ie_{j}=I_{j}e_{j}$ and $I_{j}>0$
([[pthm-cm10-principal-axes]] clauses (a) and (d)), use the model in the
**torque-free** branch of [[post-cm11-torque-balance]] clause (iv), and fix
an index $j\in\{1,2,3\}$, a rate $\Omega\in\mathbb R$, a nondegenerate open
interval $I$ ([[def-interval]]), a time $t_{0}\in I$ and an orientation
$R_{0}\in SO(3)$. Then:

1. **Existence of the uniform rotation.** There is a path
   $R:I\to SO(3)$ of class $C^{1}$ with $R(t_{0})=R_{0}$ and
   $$R(t)^{\mathsf T}R'(t)=[\Omega e_{j}]_\times\qquad(t\in I),$$
   that is, with constant body angular velocity $\omega\equiv\Omega e_{j}$
   ([[def-cm10-angular-velocity]] clause (a)).
2. **It is a torque-free motion.** For every such path $R$ and every curve
   $c:I\to\mathbb R^{3}$ of class $C^{2}$, the map
   $x(t,\rho):=c(t)+R(t)\rho$ is a motion of the torque-free model of the
   branch: its angular momentum about the centre of mass is
   $$L_c(t)=\Omega I_{j}\,R(t)e_{j},$$
   it is constant on $I$, and the adopted balance $L_c'=0$ holds. (Here $R$
   is automatically of class $C^{2}$, because $R'=R[\Omega e_{j}]_\times$ is
   the product of the $C^{1}$ curve $R$ with a constant matrix, so the
   configuration path $(c,R)$ has the regularity required of a motion.)
3. **Geometry and invariants.** In the motions of clause 2 one has
   $l=I\omega=\Omega I_{j}e_{j}$ constant,
   $$C=\lVert L_c\rVert_2^{2}=\Omega^{2}I_{j}^{2},\qquad E=\tfrac12\omega^{\mathsf T}I\omega=\tfrac12\Omega^{2}I_{j};$$
   if $\Omega\neq0$, the material axis $R(t)e_{j}$ is **fixed in the inertial
   frame**, $R(t)e_{j}=L_c/(\Omega I_{j})$ for every $t$, so the motion is a
   uniform rotation about the fixed spatial direction $L_c/|L_c|$; if
   $\Omega=0$, then $R$ is constant on $I$.
4. **Converse classification.** Conversely, let a motion of a nondegenerate
   torque-free model have **constant** body angular velocity
   $\omega\equiv\omega_{0}$ on its time window. Then
   $I\omega_{0}=\lambda\omega_{0}$ for some $\lambda\in\mathbb R$: either
   $\omega_{0}=0$ and the orientation path is constant, or $\omega_{0}\neq0$
   and $\omega_{0}$ lies along a principal axis; in the latter case
   $\omega_{0}=\Omega e_{j}$ for some $j$ and $\Omega\neq0$, and the
   conclusions of clauses 2 and 3 hold for it.

The statement is conditional on the adopted model and zero-torque balance; it
asserts no force, no measurement and no empirical law, and the existence
clause is a statement about the model's kinematic class, not about nature.
items.physical_scope: Conditional statements about the torque-free branch of a nondegenerate rigid-material model of [[post-cm10-rigid-material]]: for every principal axis $e_j$ and every real rate $\Omega$ there is a motion whose orientation path is a uniform rotation with constant body angular velocity $\Omega e_j$; for $\Omega\neq0$ the material axis $R(t)e_j$ is fixed in the inertial frame and the motion is a rotation about a fixed spatial direction; the invariants take the values $C=\Omega^{2}I_j^{2}$, $E=\tfrac12\Omega^{2}I_j$; and conversely, a torque-free motion with constant body angular velocity must spin about a principal axis. The statements carry the countable-choice assumption used only to select the initial unit quaternion, assert no measurement, no empirical law and no claim that any apparatus has been observed.

items.title: Linearization of the torque-free spin of the rigid-material model at a principal-axis spin: the oscillatory/exponential dichotomy and linear stability
items.statement:
Adopt a **nondegenerate** model of the rigid-material branch
[[post-cm10-rigid-material]] with **pairwise distinct** principal moments in
a principal basis $(e_{1},e_{2},e_{3})$, $Ie_{j}=I_{j}e_{j}$ with $I_{j}>0$
([[pthm-cm10-principal-axes]] clauses (a) and (d)), and use it in the
**torque-free** branch of [[post-cm11-torque-balance]] clause (iv). In the
body-angular-velocity variable $\omega$ the torque-free dynamics is the
autonomous field
$$F(\omega):=-I^{-1}\bigl(\omega\times I\omega\bigr),\qquad \omega\in\mathbb R^{3},$$
on $\mathbb R^{3}$ ([[pthm-cm11-euler-equations]] clause 4), and for every
axis $j$ and every $\Omega\neq0$ the constant path
$\bar\omega\equiv\Omega e_{j}$ is a solution ([[pthm-cm11-principal-rotations]]
clauses 1-3). Fix such $j$ and $\Omega$, let $\{a,b\}$ be the two indices
other than $j$, and put
$$\lambda_{j}:=\frac{\Omega^{2}\,(I_{a}-I_{j})(I_{j}-I_{b})}{I_{a}I_{b}}\neq0,\qquad \kappa_{j}:=\sqrt{\lvert\lambda_{j}\rvert}.$$
Then:

1. **The linearized field.** $F$ is totally differentiable at $\Omega e_{j}$
   in the sense of [[def-total-derivative-in-euclidean-space]], with total
   derivative $A_{j}$ given on the principal basis by
   $$A_{j}e_{a}=\frac{\Omega(I_{b}-I_{j})}{I_{a}}\,e_{b},\qquad A_{j}e_{b}=\frac{\Omega(I_{j}-I_{a})}{I_{b}}\,e_{a},\qquad A_{j}e_{j}=0,$$
   and there is a constant $C\ge0$ with
   $\lVert F(\Omega e_{j}+\delta)-A_{j}\delta\rVert_2\le C\lVert\delta\rVert_2^{2}$
   for all $\delta\in\mathbb R^{3}$.
2. **The linearized system and its dichotomy.** Write
   $\delta=\delta_{a}e_{a}+\delta_{b}e_{b}+\delta_{j}e_{j}$.
   - If $I_{j}$ is a **largest or smallest** principal moment, then
     $\lambda_{j}<0$, every solution of the linearized system
     $\delta'=A_{j}\delta$ is defined on all of $\mathbb R$ and bounded on
     $[0,\infty)$, with
     $$\delta_{a}(t)=\delta_{a}(0)\cos(\kappa_{j}t)+\frac{\Omega(I_{b}-I_{j})}{I_{a}\kappa_{j}}\,\delta_{b}(0)\sin(\kappa_{j}t),$$
     $$\delta_{b}(t)=\delta_{b}(0)\cos(\kappa_{j}t)+\frac{\Omega(I_{j}-I_{a})}{I_{b}\kappa_{j}}\,\delta_{a}(0)\sin(\kappa_{j}t),$$
     and $\delta_{j}$ constant; consequently the spin is **linearly stable** in
     the sense of [[def-cm-orbital-and-linear-stability]].
   - If $I_{j}$ lies **strictly between** $I_{a}$ and $I_{b}$, then
     $\lambda_{j}>0$, the same two formulas hold with $\cosh$ and $\sinh$ in
     place of $\cos$ and $\sin$ and $\kappa_{j}=\sqrt{\lambda_{j}}$, the
     linearized system has unbounded solutions (for instance with
     $\delta_{b}(0)=0$ and $\delta_{a}(0)\neq0$ satisfying
     $\delta_{a}(0)+\frac{\Omega(I_{b}-I_{j})}{I_{a}\kappa_{j}}\delta_{b}(0)\neq0$),
     and the spin is **not linearly stable**.

The statement is a statement about the linearized system at the spin; the
corresponding nonlinear Lyapunov statements are separate items of this page,
and no conclusion about the nonlinear stability of the spin is drawn here.

items.title: Nonlinear stability of the torque-free spin of the rigid-material model about an extreme principal axis, and instability about the intermediate axis, with an explicit escape time and the orientation caveat
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]), used only to select initial unit quaternions
through the double cover of [[def-cm-quaternion-rotation-map-and-cover]].
Adopt a **nondegenerate** model of the rigid-material branch
[[post-cm10-rigid-material]] with pairwise distinct principal moments, and
label a principal basis $(e_{1},e_{2},e_{3})$, $Ie_{j}=I_{j}e_{j}$, so that
$$I_{1}<I_{2}<I_{3}.$$
Use the model in the **torque-free** branch of [[post-cm11-torque-balance]]
clause (iv). Along any motion write $l:=I\omega$; the torque-free $l$-path
solves $l'=l\times(I^{-1}l)$ and is the restriction of a solution defined on
all of $\mathbb R$ ([[pthm-cm11-torque-free-invariants]] clauses 2 and 4).
Let $L\neq0$. Then:

1. **Stability of the extreme-axis spins.** For $j=1$ and $j=3$ the constant
   path $t\mapsto Le_{j}$ is Lyapunov stable for the $l$-system
   ([[def-cm-equilibrium-and-lyapunov-stability]]): for every $\varepsilon>0$
   there is $\delta\in(0,\varepsilon]$ such that every solution $l$ with
   $\lVert l(0)-Le_{j}\rVert_2<\delta$ is defined for all $t\ge0$ and
   satisfies $\lVert l(t)-Le_{j}\rVert_2<\varepsilon$ for all $t\ge0$.
   Consequently every torque-free motion of a model of the branch whose time
   window contains $[0,\infty)$ and whose datum satisfies
   $\lVert l(0)-Le_{j}\rVert_2<\delta$ has, with $\Omega:=L/I_{j}$,
   $$\lVert l(t)-Le_{j}\rVert_2<\varepsilon,\qquad \lVert\omega(t)-\Omega e_{j}\rVert_2<\frac{\varepsilon}{I_{\min}}\qquad(t\ge0),$$
   where $I_{\min}=I_{1}$.
2. **Explicit deviation bound.** For $j=1$ define on $\mathbb R^{3}$
   $$c_{1}:=\tfrac12\Bigl(\frac1{I_{1}}-\frac1{I_{2}}\Bigr)>0,\qquad D_{1}(l):=\tfrac12\Bigl(\frac{\langle l,l\rangle}{I_{1}}-\langle l,I^{-1}l\rangle\Bigr)\ \ge0,$$
   and for $j=3$
   $$c_{3}:=\tfrac12\Bigl(\frac1{I_{2}}-\frac1{I_{3}}\Bigr)>0,\qquad D_{3}(l):=\tfrac12\Bigl(\langle l,I^{-1}l\rangle-\frac{\langle l,l\rangle}{I_{3}}\Bigr)\ \ge0.$$
   Along every solution of $l'=l\times(I^{-1}l)$ one has, for all $t$ in its
   interval,
   $$l_{2}(t)^{2}+l_{3}(t)^{2}\le\frac{D_{1}(l(0))}{c_{1}},\qquad l_{1}(t)^{2}+l_{2}(t)^{2}\le\frac{D_{3}(l(0))}{c_{3}}.$$
3. **Instability of the intermediate-axis spin.** The spin $l_{0}:=Le_{2}$ is
   not Lyapunov stable. More precisely, with
   $$a:=\sqrt{\frac{1/I_{1}-1/I_{2}}{1/I_{2}-1/I_{3}}}>0,\qquad c_{0}:=a\Bigl(\frac1{I_{2}}-\frac1{I_{3}}\Bigr)\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\,\lvert L\rvert>0,\qquad \delta_{0}:=\frac{\lvert L\rvert}{2\sqrt{1+a^{2}}},\qquad \varepsilon_{0}:=\frac{\lvert L\rvert}{2},$$
   for every $\delta>0$ there are a torque-free **motion** of the model with
   time window containing $[0,\infty)$, with body angular velocity $\omega$,
   and a time $t\ge0$ such that
   $$\lVert l(0)-Le_{2}\rVert_2<\delta,\qquad \lVert l(t)-Le_{2}\rVert_2\ge\varepsilon_{0},$$
   and the escape can be arranged with $t\le c_{0}^{-1}\log(\delta_{0}/\eta)$
   for any prescribed $\eta\in(0,\min\{\delta_{0},\delta\})$ with the initial
   datum $l^{\eta}:=\bigl(\eta,\ \sigma\sqrt{L^{2}-(1+a^{2})\eta^{2}},\ -\sigma a\eta\bigr)$,
   $\sigma:=L/\lvert L\rvert$, of the $l$-system.
4. **Orientation caveat.** For $j=1$ or $j=3$ and every $\Omega\neq0$ there
   are two torque-free motions of the model, with $c\equiv0$, whose body
   angular velocities are both constantly equal to $\Omega e_{j}$ and whose
   orientation paths $R_{1},R_{2}$ satisfy $R_{2}(t)=R_{1}(t)S$ for every $t$
   and a fixed rotation $S\neq I_{3}$. Consequently clause 1 asserts nothing
   about the closeness of the orientations of two motions.

The statement is conditional on the adopted model and zero-torque balance; it
asserts no force, no damping, no measurement and no empirical law.
items.physical_scope: Lyapunov stability and instability of the torque-free spin of a nondegenerate rigid-material model of [[post-cm10-rigid-material]] with pairwise distinct principal moments, stated for the model's motions with time window containing $[0,\infty)$: spins about the largest and smallest principal axes are Lyapunov stable in the body angular momentum, with an explicit conserved deviation bound, and spins about the intermediate axis are unstable with an explicit escape time; the escaping perturbation is realised by an actual torque-free motion. The stability is a statement about the body-frame angular momentum and angular velocity only: two motions with the same constant body angular velocity can have orientations differing by a fixed nontrivial rotation at every time, so no orientation stability is asserted. No measurement, damping, dissipation or empirical value is asserted; the countable-choice assumption is carried for the quaternion constructions.

items.title: Adoption of the heavy symmetric top branch: axisymmetric rigid material, a fixed pivot material point, a uniform gravitational field and the balance of angular momentum about the pivot
items.statement:
Adopt as physical assumptions of the framework the following **heavy symmetric
top branch** of the rigid-material model, in the setting of
[[post-cm10-rigid-material]].

**(i) Setting.** A model of the branch carries the data of
[[post-cm10-rigid-material]]: a reference mass distribution $\nu$ with total
mass $m>0$ and centred reference coordinates, a time window $I_0$, an
inertial frame with adapted coordinates $(t,x)$ ([[post-cm01-frames]]),
whose origin is chosen at the pivot point of clause (iii), and a motion
$x(t,\rho)=c(t)+R(t)\rho$ with configuration path $(c,R)$ of class $C^{2}$
([[def-cm10-rigid-body-configuration]]). Assume the Axiom of Countable
Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]), used only through the
integrals of the model's inertial quantities. Fix once and for all an
orthonormal basis $(e_{1},e_{2},e_{3})$ of the reference coordinates.

**(ii) Axisymmetry and the declared parameters.** The body inertia matrix of
the model ([[def-cm10-inertia-tensor]] clause (a)) is
$$I=A_{c}\,(e_{1}e_{1}^{\mathsf T}+e_{2}e_{2}^{\mathsf T})+C_{c}\,e_{3}e_{3}^{\mathsf T},\qquad A_{c}>0,\ C_{c}>0,$$
so that $e_{3}$ is the **symmetry axis**; the numbers $A_{c}$, $C_{c}$ are
declared model parameters of dimension $\mu\ell^{2}$, read in kilogram metres
squared, and are not measured within the framework. The branch also declares
a **pivot distance** $d>0$ of dimension $\ell$ and a **field strength**
$g>0$ of dimension $\ell\tau^{-2}$, read in metres per second squared
([[def-cm01-units]]).

**(iii) The pivot constraint.** The material point of reference coordinate
$\rho_{p}:=-d\,e_{3}$ is the **pivot material point**; it lies on the
symmetry axis at distance $d$ from the centre of mass. The motions of the
branch are those satisfying
$$c(t)+R(t)\rho_{p}=0\qquad(t\in I_{0}),$$
that is $c(t)=d\,R(t)e_{3}$: the pivot material point is held fixed at the
origin of the inertial frame for the whole time window, and the centre of
mass is constrained to the circle of radius $d$ about the origin. The
constraint is maintained by a mechanism (a bearing, a hinge or a fine
support) whose force system is **ideal** in the sense adopted for
frictionless hinges in [[post-cm06-ideal-reaction-law]] clause (iii) together
with the virtual-work law of its clause (i): the mechanism exerts on the body
a force system equivalent to a single force applied at the pivot point, so
that its total torque about the origin **vanishes**. The holonomic-constraint
vocabulary of [[def-cm06-holonomic-constraint-model]] — constrained curve
families, reaction fields and the declaration that the constraint is
maintained by an additional force contribution — is the framework's account
for finitely many particle labels; the present model is a continuum, and this
clause adopts the analogous idealisation for it. No friction, damping or
driving torque at the pivot is asserted; such torques are excluded and would
have to be declared as part of a torque datum with their own model.

**(iv) The uniform gravitational field.** The model declares a **uniform
gravitational acceleration** $G:=-g\,e_{3}$ of dimension $\ell\tau^{-2}$:
every material point of the body is subject to the external force
$G\,d\nu$, that is, the force per unit mass is the constant vector $-g e_{3}$
([[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]] for the
spatial vectors). The field is a model idealisation: it asserts neither a
particular direction in any absolute sense (the direction $e_{3}$ is a
declared frame direction) nor a measured value of $g$, and it is not
asserted to represent the Earth's or any planet's field. The resultant of
this force system and its total torque about a point are computed in
the reduction theorem of this page; in particular the resultant is the total weight
$-mg e_{3}$ applied at the centre of mass.

**(v) The adopted dynamics.** Along every motion of the branch adopt the
**balance of angular momentum about the pivot**: with
$$J_{p}(t):=\int\bigl(x(t,\rho)-0\bigr)\times\partial_{t}x(t,\rho)\,d\nu(\rho)$$
the angular momentum of the model about the origin, and with $\tau_{p}(t)$
the total external torque about the origin — the sum of the gravitational
torque and of the pivot reaction torque, the latter vanishing by clause
(iii) — adopt
$$J_{p}'(t)=\tau_{p}(t)\qquad(t\in I_{0}).$$
This is an adopted dynamical law of the branch, analogous to but distinct
from the balance of [[post-cm11-torque-balance]] clause (iii) about the
centre of mass; it acquires content only together with the kinematic
constraint of clause (iii) and the external force system of clause (iv). No
equation of motion for the pivot reaction is asserted: the reaction is
whatever force the ideal mechanism supplies, and its torque about the origin
is zero by clause (iii).

**(vi) Scope and exclusions.** The branch excludes non-axisymmetric bodies
($A_{c}$ and $C_{c}$ are the two transverse and the axial moment and no other
inertia data are used), bodies whose mass distribution fails to produce this
inertia matrix, non-uniform gravitational fields, friction and driving
torques at the pivot, rolling or sliding contacts, impacts, deformable
bodies and variable mass, and every relativistic or quantum description. It
asserts no force law for the pivot reaction, no conservation law and no
measured value of $A_{c}$, $C_{c}$, $m$, $d$ or $g$. Whether the branch is
adequate for a given apparatus — a top on a bearing, a gyroscope in a gimbal,
a spinning shell — is decided by comparing the model's conditional
predictions with reported observations of that apparatus under its stated
regime, and agreement is evidence about the combined model and apparatus, not
a proof of the idealisation.

**(vii) Relation to the other balances.** The balance of clause (v) is not
claimed to be a consequence of the centre-of-mass balance of
[[post-cm11-torque-balance]] clause (iii), nor conversely; the two are
separate adopted laws about different points, and neither is deduced from the
framework's particle balances. A model may use both simultaneously, and the
reduction theorem of this page uses only clause (v) together with clauses
(ii)-(iv).
items.physical_scope: Adoption of the heavy symmetric top branch of the rigid-material model: a reference mass distribution whose body inertia matrix is diag(A_c,A_c,C_c) about a declared symmetry axis, a material point held fixed at the origin of the inertial frame (the pivot, on the symmetry axis at distance d from the centre of mass, so that the centre of mass is constrained to the circle of radius d about the pivot), an ideal pivot mechanism contributing no torque about the pivot in the framework's sense of a frictionless hinge, a uniform gravitational field of magnitude g directed along $-e_3$, and the adopted balance of angular momentum about the pivot. The branch excludes friction and driving torques at the pivot, rolling and sliding contacts, non-axisymmetric bodies and non-uniform fields, and asserts no measured value and no claim that a concrete top or gyroscope realises it.

items.title: Reduction of the heavy symmetric top branch: pivotal angular momentum, Euler-angle equations, the two conserved momenta and the one-dimensional $\theta$ equation
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]), used only for the finiteness of the defining
integrals of the model's inertial quantities. Adopt the heavy symmetric top
branch [[post-cm11-heavy-top]] with parameters $A_{c}>0$, $C_{c}>0$, $d>0$,
$g>0$ and total mass $m>0$; use the notation of that postulate: the pivot
material point $\rho_{p}=-d\,e_{3}$ is held at the origin, so
$c(t)=d\,R(t)e_{3}$; the pivot reaction contributes no torque about the
origin; and the external gravitational field is $G=-g e_{3}$ with total
torque about the origin $\tau_{p}(t)=-mgd\,(R(t)e_{3})\times e_{3}$. Put
$$A:=A_{c}+md^{2}>0,\qquad C:=C_{c}>0,$$
the transverse moment of the model about the pivot and its axial moment. Let
$x(t,\rho)=c(t)+R(t)\rho$ be a motion of the branch with time window $I_0$,
and suppose that there are functions $\varphi,\theta,\psi:I_0\to\mathbb R$
of class $C^{2}$ with $\theta(I_0)\subseteq(0,\pi)$ and
$$R(t)=\Theta\bigl(\varphi(t),\theta(t),\psi(t)\bigr)=R_{z}\bigl(\varphi(t)\bigr)R_{y}\bigl(\theta(t)\bigr)R_{z}\bigl(\psi(t)\bigr)\qquad(t\in I_0),$$
the Euler-angle description of [[def-cm-euler-angle-parametrization-and-heavy-top-system]].
Then:

1. **Angular momentum about the pivot.** With $\omega$ the body angular
   velocity of the motion and
   $\tilde I:=A\,(e_{1}e_{1}^{\mathsf T}+e_{2}e_{2}^{\mathsf T})+C\,e_{3}e_{3}^{\mathsf T}$
   (the diagonal matrix $\mathrm{diag}(A,A,C)$ in the principal basis) one has
   $$J_{p}(t):=\int x(t,\rho)\times\partial_{t}x(t,\rho)\,d\nu(\rho)=R(t)\,\tilde I\,\omega(t),$$
   and the balance of [[post-cm11-heavy-top]] clause (v) reads
   $J_{p}'=\tau_{p}$ with
   $$\tau_{p}(t)=-mgd\,\bigl(R(t)e_{3}\bigr)\times e_{3},\qquad \tau_{p}(t)\cdot e_{3}=0 .$$
2. **Body-frame pivot equations.** With $\gamma(t):=R(t)^{\mathsf T}e_{3}$,
   $$\tilde I\,\omega'+\omega\times\tilde I\,\omega=-mgd\,\bigl(e_{3}\times\gamma\bigr)\qquad\text{on }I_0,$$
   that is, componentwise in the principal basis,
   $$A\omega_{1}'=(A-C)\omega_{2}\omega_{3}+mgd\,\gamma_{2},\qquad A\omega_{2}'=(C-A)\omega_{1}\omega_{3}-mgd\,\gamma_{1},\qquad C\omega_{3}'=0 .$$
   Under the Euler-angle description of the statement,
   $$\gamma=\bigl(-\sin\theta\cos\psi,\ \sin\theta\sin\psi,\ \cos\theta\bigr),\qquad \omega_{3}=\psi'+\varphi'\cos\theta .$$
3. **Reduction to one dimension.** Define on $I_0$
   $$b:=C\bigl(\psi'+\varphi'\cos\theta\bigr),\qquad a:=A\,\varphi'\sin^{2}\theta+b\cos\theta .$$
   Then $b$ and $a$ are constant on $I_0$; consequently
   $$\varphi'=\frac{a-b\cos\theta}{A\sin^{2}\theta},\qquad \psi'=\frac{b}{C}-\frac{(a-b\cos\theta)\cos\theta}{A\sin^{2}\theta};$$
   the **reduced energy**
   $$E:=\tfrac12 A\,\theta'^{2}+\frac{(a-b\cos\theta)^{2}}{2A\sin^{2}\theta}+\frac{b^{2}}{2C}+mgd\cos\theta$$
   is constant on $I_0$; and with the **effective potential**
   $$U(\theta):=\frac{(a-b\cos\theta)^{2}}{2A\sin^{2}\theta}+\frac{b^{2}}{2C}+mgd\cos\theta$$
   one has $A\,\theta''=-U'(\theta)$ on $I_0$.
4. **The heavy-top system.** Equivalently, $(\varphi,\theta,\psi)$ is a
   heavy-top trajectory of [[def-cm-euler-angle-parametrization-and-heavy-top-system]]
   with parameters $(A,C,m,d,g)$, and clauses 1-4 of
   [[thm-cm-heavy-top-reduction]] hold for it.

The statement assumes the Euler-angle description as a hypothesis on the
interval: no claim is made that every motion of the branch admits such a
description, that a description extends across the poles $\theta\in\{0,\pi\}$
(where the sleeping-top and hanging configurations lie), or that the
description is unique. On every subinterval on which a description with
$\theta\in(0,\pi)$ exists, the conclusions hold there. The statement asserts
no friction or driving torque at the pivot, no measurement and no empirical
value.
items.physical_scope: Conditional deductions inside the heavy symmetric top branch of [[post-cm11-heavy-top]] for the rigid-material model of [[post-cm10-rigid-material]]: the angular momentum about the pivot equals $R\tilde I\omega$ with $\tilde I$ the inertia about the pivot; the pivot balance gives the body-frame equations; and on any interval on which the orientation is described by the Euler-angle chart with $\theta\in(0,\pi)$ the motion satisfies the heavy-top system with parameters equal to the pivot transverse moment $A=A_c+md^{2}$, the axial moment $C=C_c$, the total mass $m$, the pivot distance $d$ and the field strength $g$, so the conserved momenta, the reduced energy and the one-dimensional $\theta$ equation hold. The statement carries the countable-choice assumption used only for the finiteness of the defining integrals, assumes the chart description as an explicit hypothesis, asserts nothing at the chart's poles, excludes friction and driving torques at the pivot, and asserts no measured value.

items.title: Two explicit free-rotation models checked: principal-axis spins, a non-uniform symmetric-top motion with its invariants, and the linearized frequencies of an asymmetric top
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]), used only through the quaternion constructions
below. Consider two **declared** models of the rigid-material branch
[[post-cm10-rigid-material]], each with body inertia matrix diagonal in the
declared orthonormal basis $(e_{1},e_{2},e_{3})$ and no other inertia data,
each used in the torque-free branch of [[post-cm11-torque-balance]] clause
(iv):

- **Model S** (symmetric): $I=\mathrm{diag}(1,1,2)$ in kilogram metres
  squared in the declared units ([[def-cm01-units]]); the principal moments
  are $I_{1}=I_{2}=1$, $I_{3}=2$.
- **Model A** (asymmetric): $I=\mathrm{diag}(1,2,3)$; the principal moments
  are $I_{1}=1<I_{2}=2<I_{3}=3$.

Verify the following.

1. **Principal-axis spins.** For each model, each $j$ and each $\Omega\in\mathbb R$,
   the constant path $\omega\equiv\Omega e_{j}$ is the body angular velocity
   of a torque-free motion; along it $l=\Omega I_{j}e_{j}$ is constant,
   $C=\Omega^{2}I_{j}^{2}$ and $E=\tfrac12\Omega^{2}I_{j}$. In Model S with
   $j=3$ and $\Omega=2$ this gives $l=4e_{3}$, $C=16$, $E=4$; in Model A with
   $j=1$ and $\Omega=1$ it gives $l=e_{1}$, $C=1$, $E=\tfrac12$.
2. **A non-uniform symmetric-top motion.** For Model S the path
   $$\omega(t)=\bigl(\tfrac12\cos t,\ \tfrac12\sin t,\ 1\bigr)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R)$$
   satisfies the torque-free Euler equations
   $l'=l\times(I^{-1}l)$ and is the body angular velocity of a torque-free
   motion of Model S; along it
   $$l(t)=\bigl(\tfrac12\cos t,\ \tfrac12\sin t,\ 2\bigr),\qquad C=\frac{17}{4},\qquad E=\frac98,\qquad\lVert\omega(t)\rVert_2^{2}=\frac54,$$
   and $\omega$ is not constant: $\omega(\tfrac\pi2)-\omega(0)=(-\tfrac12,\tfrac12,0)$.
3. **Linearization of Model A at its principal-axis spins.** At the spin
   $\Omega e_{1}$ with $\Omega=1$ the linearized system of
   [[pthm-cm11-linearized-spin]] has $\lambda_{1}=-\tfrac13$, $\kappa_{1}=1/\sqrt3$, and the
   pair $(\delta_{2},\delta_{3})=(\cos(t/\sqrt3),\ -\tfrac1{\sqrt3}\sin(t/\sqrt3))$
   solves the transverse equations; at the intermediate spin $e_{2}$ with
   $\Omega=1$ the linearized system has $\lambda_{2}=\tfrac13>0$ and the
   solution with $\delta_{1}(0)=1$, $\delta_{3}(0)=0$ has $\delta_{1}(t)=\cosh(t/\sqrt3)$,
   which is unbounded on $[0,\infty)$; at the extreme spin $e_{3}$ with
   $\Omega=1$ one has $\kappa_{3}=1$.

The checks verify principal-axis spins and their invariants, an explicit non-uniform symmetric-top motion with conserved angular momentum and energy, and the linearized frequencies at the principal-axis spins of the asymmetric model. No measured value, no concrete body and no experiment is asserted; the numerical data are declared model parameters.

items.title: A torque-free motion of a symmetric rigid-material model with constant angular momentum and energy whose body angular velocity is not constant: the invariants do not force a uniform rotation
items.statement:
Let a model of the rigid-material branch [[post-cm10-rigid-material]] be used
in the **torque-free** branch of [[post-cm11-torque-balance]] clause (iv), and
let $x(t,\rho)=c(t)+R(t)\rho$ be a motion of the resulting model on a time
window containing $[0,\infty)$. Suppose that along the motion the angular
momentum about the centre of mass $L_c$ and the rotational kinetic energy
$\tfrac12\omega^{\mathsf T}I\omega$ are constant in time. Then the body
angular velocity $\omega$ of the motion is constant in time.
items.physical_scope: A refutation inside the torque-free branch of the rigid-material model of [[post-cm10-rigid-material]]: on the declared symmetric model with body inertia matrix diag(1,1,2) there is a torque-free motion whose angular momentum about the centre of mass and rotational kinetic energy are both constant while its body angular velocity varies with time. The item refutes only the displayed false statement; it asserts no measurement, no concrete body and no failure of the torque-free equations, of which the exhibited motion is an exact solution.

items.title: Explicit escape from the intermediate-axis spin of the model with inertia diag(1,2,3): the constants, the perturbed invariant level, and the escape-time bound
items.statement:
Adopt the **model A** of [[ex-cm11-free-top-checks]]: the rigid-material
model of [[post-cm10-rigid-material]] with body inertia matrix
$I=\mathrm{diag}(1,2,3)$ in the declared orthonormal basis, used in the
torque-free branch of [[post-cm11-torque-balance]] clause (iv). Its principal
moments are $I_{1}=1<I_{2}=2<I_{3}=3$
([[pthm-cm10-principal-axes]] clauses (a) and (d)). Take the intermediate-axis
spin datum $l_{0}:=Le_{2}$ with $L=1$, and let $q:=\tfrac1{400}$ and
$$l^{q}:=\Bigl(q,\ \sqrt{1-4q^{2}},\ -\sqrt3\,q\Bigr),$$
so that $q=1/400$ and $\sqrt{1-4q^{2}}=\sqrt{159999/160000}$. Verify:

1. **The instability constants of [[pthm-cm11-nonlinear-spin-stability]] clause 3.**

$$a=\sqrt3,\qquad c_{0}=\frac14,\qquad \delta_{0}=\frac14,\qquad \varepsilon_{0}=\frac12 .$$

2. **The perturbed datum lies on the invariant level of the spin.**
   $C(l^{q})=C(l_{0})=1$ and $E(l^{q})=E(l_{0})=\tfrac14$, where
   $C(z)=\langle z,z\rangle$ and $E(z)=\tfrac12\langle z,I^{-1}z\rangle$ are
   the invariants of [[pthm-cm11-torque-free-invariants]] clause 2.
3. **The perturbed datum is close to the spin.** $\lVert l^{q}-l_{0}\rVert_2<\tfrac1{100}$
   and $q<\min\{\delta_{0},\tfrac1{100}\}$.
4. **The escape.** There is a torque-free motion of model A whose $l$-path has
   $l(0)=l^{q}$ and satisfies
   $$\lVert l(0)-e_{2}\rVert_2<\tfrac1{100},\qquad \lVert l(t)-e_{2}\rVert_2\ge\tfrac12$$
   at some time $0\le t\le4\log 100\approx18.42$; in particular the
   intermediate-axis spin $e_{2}$ of model A is not Lyapunov stable, with an
   explicit effective escape at the displayed constants.
items.physical_scope: A worked instance of the intermediate-axis instability of [[pthm-cm11-nonlinear-spin-stability]] on the declared model with body inertia matrix diag(1,2,3) and spin datum $l_0=e_2$: the instability constants, a perturbed datum on the same invariant level with the checked proximity bound, and the resulting escape time and escape radius. The numerical data are declared model parameters; no measurement, no concrete body and no experiment is asserted.

items.title: A steady precession of the heavy symmetric top checked on explicit data: the pivot balance, the two conserved momenta and the reduced energy
items.statement:
Adopt the heavy symmetric top branch [[post-cm11-heavy-top]] with declared
parameters
$$A_{c}=2,\qquad C_{c}=1,\qquad m=1,\qquad d=1,\qquad g=1$$
in the framework's units ([[def-cm01-units]]), so that the body inertia
matrix is $I=\mathrm{diag}(2,2,1)$ in the declared basis and the pivot
transverse moment is
$$A=A_{c}+md^{2}=2+1=3,\qquad C=C_{c}=1 .$$
Let $\theta_{0}:=\pi/3$ and consider the angles
$$\varphi(t)=t,\qquad\theta(t)=\theta_{0},\qquad\psi(t)=2t\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),$$
the orientation path $R(t):=\Theta(\varphi(t),\theta(t),\psi(t))$ of
[[def-cm-euler-angle-parametrization-and-heavy-top-system]], the centre of
mass $c(t):=d\,R(t)e_{3}$, and the motion $x(t,\rho):=c(t)+R(t)\rho$. Verify:

1. **It is a motion of the branch satisfying the pivot balance.** The pivot
   constraint $c(t)+R(t)(-de_{3})=0$ holds, and with
   $\omega(t)=\bigl(-\tfrac{\sqrt3}2\cos(2t),\ \tfrac{\sqrt3}2\sin(2t),\ \tfrac52\bigr)$
   and $\gamma(t)=R(t)^{\mathsf T}e_{3}$,
   $$\tilde I\,\omega'+\omega\times\tilde I\,\omega=-mgd\,(e_{3}\times\gamma)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),$$
   where $\tilde I=\mathrm{diag}(3,3,1)$; hence the motion satisfies the
   adopted balance of [[post-cm11-heavy-top]] clause (v) and the conclusions
   of [[pthm-cm11-top-reduction]] clauses 1-2 hold along it.
2. **The conserved momenta and the reduced energy.** With
   $\varphi'=1$, $\theta'=0$, $\psi'=2$,
   $$a=A\varphi'\sin^{2}\theta_{0}+b\cos\theta_{0}=\frac72,\qquad b=C\bigl(\psi'+\varphi'\cos\theta_{0}\bigr)=\frac52,\qquad E=U(\theta_{0})=\frac{19}{4}.$$
3. **The heavy-top system holds, and $\theta$ is constant.** The three
   equations of [[def-cm-euler-angle-parametrization-and-heavy-top-system]]
   hold for the triple, and $A\theta''=-U'(\theta_{0})=0$, so the motion is a
   **steady precession**: $\varphi'=1$ and $\psi'=2$ are constant and the
   nutation angle is constantly $\pi/3$.
items.physical_scope: A worked steady precession of the heavy symmetric top branch of [[post-cm11-heavy-top]] on declared parameters $A_c=2$, $C_c=1$, $m=1$, $d=1$, $g=1$ (so the pivot transverse moment is $A=3$) and the explicit angles $\varphi(t)=t$, $\theta=\pi/3$, $\psi(t)=2t$: the pivot balance is verified identically in time, the two conserved momenta are $a=7/2$ and $b=5/2$, the reduced energy is $19/4$, and the heavy-top system holds, so the reduction conclusions apply. All numbers are declared model data in the framework's units; no measurement, no concrete top and no experiment is asserted.
